resume: Seventies string ensemble, grown out of OberVave: one key, one keyer, registers (double bass, cello, viola, violin, trumpet, horn), a delay-line ensemble and a phaser per sound. Four tracks, a mixer, a MASTER and a sequencer.

commandes.role: Octave down; with OCT+, back to 0. With EDIT, undo.
Octave up; with OCT-, back to 0. With EDIT, redo.
Tapped: ENSEMBLE, PHASER, DELAY, REVERB, DRIVE. Held: effects layer, the keys play notes.
KEYER page: ATTACK, RELEASE, VELOCITY, GLIDE.
Tapped: STRINGS (the string registers), BRASS + SPLIT, TONE; in STEPS, clears the step. Held: erases the note played.
Tapped: GLOBAL, OUTPUT. Held: the white keys start, mute or solo tracks A to D.
PERFORM page (TONE, ATTACK, RELEASE, DEPTH of the ensemble); again, the MIXER.
Twice: saves the track's program. Held: goes to a pattern (white keys 1 to 8) or copies it (black).
Arpeggiator page; on this page, ARP becomes HOLD.
Tapped: full-screen sequencer, then its views (TRACKS, STEPS, TRACK, PATTERNS). Held: the keys are the steps.
Starts the active tracks from step 1, or stops them.
While playing, records the selected track; when stopped, arms (the first note starts). Held 1.2 s: erases the track.
Tempo; in the sequencer and the mixer, the next pattern (on the bar).
Chooses the track, A to D.
They play the sound of the selected track.

a_savoir: Four full string sounds cost about twice the processor of a single one: watch the CPU time on the GLOBAL page.
